# Neovim

> Neovim is a hyperextensible, Vim-based text editor. It seeks to aggressively
> refactor Vim in order to: simplify maintenance and encourage contributions,
> split the work between multiple developers, enable advanced UIs without
> modifications to the core, and maximize extensibility via a msgpack-based
> RPC API used for a built-in Lua scripting engine and remote plugins in any
> language.

## Getting Started

- [Homepage](https://neovim.io/): overview, editions, and quick links.
- [Install](https://neovim.io/doc/install/): installation instructions for all platforms.
- [About](https://neovim.io/about/): project background and goals.
- [Charter](https://neovim.io/charter/): governance and project principles.
- [Roadmap](https://neovim.io/roadmap/): planned work and priorities.

## Core Reference

- [Documentation Index](https://neovim.io/doc/): full generated Vim/Nvim help index.
- [Quick Reference](https://neovim.io/doc/user/quickref/): condensed command and option reference.
- [Options](https://neovim.io/doc/user/options/): all editor options.
- [User Functions](https://neovim.io/doc/user/userfunc/): Vimscript function reference.
- [Vim Differences](https://neovim.io/doc/user/vim_diff/): where Nvim intentionally differs from Vim.
- [Introduction](https://neovim.io/doc/user/intro/): basic concepts and notation used across the docs.

## Editing and Navigation

- [Editing](https://neovim.io/doc/user/editing/): editing files, buffers, and windows.
- [Motion](https://neovim.io/doc/user/motion/): cursor movement commands.
- [Insert Mode](https://neovim.io/doc/user/insert/): insert and replace mode commands.
- [Change](https://neovim.io/doc/user/change/): deleting and changing text.
- [Visual Mode](https://neovim.io/doc/user/visual/): visual selection commands.
- [Windows](https://neovim.io/doc/user/windows/): window layout and management.
- [Tab Pages](https://neovim.io/doc/user/tabpage/): tab page management.
- [Command-Line](https://neovim.io/doc/user/cmdline/): command-line mode and commands.
- [Autocommands](https://neovim.io/doc/user/autocmd/): event-driven automation.
- [Repeat](https://neovim.io/doc/user/repeat/): repeating and undo/redo commands.
- [Undo](https://neovim.io/doc/user/undo/): undo tree.
- [Folding](https://neovim.io/doc/user/fold/): code folding.
- [Diff Mode](https://neovim.io/doc/user/diff/): file comparison.
- [Terminal](https://neovim.io/doc/user/terminal/): built-in terminal emulator.

## Scripting and Extensibility

- [Lua Guide](https://neovim.io/doc/user/lua-guide/): practical introduction to configuring/scripting Nvim in Lua.
- [Lua Reference](https://neovim.io/doc/user/lua/): full Lua API reference.
- [API](https://neovim.io/doc/user/api/): msgpack-RPC API reference used by UIs and remote plugins.
- [UI Events](https://neovim.io/doc/user/api-ui-events/): UI protocol events.
- [Remote Plugins](https://neovim.io/doc/user/remote_plugin/): writing plugins in any language via RPC.
- [Providers](https://neovim.io/doc/user/provider/): Python/Ruby/Node provider integrations.
- [Packages](https://neovim.io/doc/user/pack/): native package/plugin loading.

## Built-in Tooling

- [LSP](https://neovim.io/doc/user/lsp/): built-in Language Server Protocol client.
- [Diagnostic](https://neovim.io/doc/user/diagnostic/): diagnostics framework shared by LSP and linters.
- [Treesitter](https://neovim.io/doc/user/treesitter/): built-in incremental parsing and syntax highlighting.
- [Spell Checking](https://neovim.io/doc/user/spell/): spell-check support.
- [Syntax Highlighting](https://neovim.io/doc/user/syntax/): legacy syntax highlighting.

## Developer Docs

- [Development](https://neovim.io/doc/user/dev/): guide for contributing to Nvim itself.
- [Development Style](https://neovim.io/doc/user/dev_style/): code style guidelines.
- [Development Architecture](https://neovim.io/doc/user/dev_arch/): high-level architecture notes.
- [Development Tools](https://neovim.io/doc/user/dev_tools/): debugging and profiling tools.
